newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open flat, selling sentiment seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open flat, selling sentiment seen.

text.p: Singapore shares opened flat on Wednesday with selling sentiment high, dealers said.
"There's quite a lot of selling out there again," a dealer with a local brokerage said.
Corporate results and jitters over economic data due from the United States later in the day and from Singapore on Thursday kept pressure firm, the dealers said.

Even so, the key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) rose 1.42 points at 0225 GMT to 2,125.71 although early losers headed gainers 124 to 61. The STII gain resulted mainly from a rise of Singapore $0.30 to S$14.60 for index counter Cycle & Carriage.
But the UOB over-the-counter index tracking mainly Malaysian stocks was down 3.58 at 1,298.14 as investor concern lingered over a diplomatic row between Singapore and Malaysia.

The row, over criticism of a Malaysian state by Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew for which he has issued an unreserved apology, was to be discussed at a Malaysian cabinet meeting later on Wednesday.
Early volume was a slim 40 million shares with DBS Bank foreign stock heading losers down S$0.20 at S$17.40 and UOB Bank foreign shares leading gainers up S$0.30 at S$16.00.
